questions.q: Why are the gate floors and drift thresholds written into params.yaml before the pipeline code is built?
options: YAML files make the model train faster
So the pass/fail rules are decided in advance and can be changed by a reviewed edit to one file
MLflow requires a params.yaml file to start
So the thresholds are hidden from reviewers
questions.explain: Deciding what good enough means before seeing results stops you from moving the goalposts, and keeping it in one file means code and reviewers read the same numbers.

questions.q: Which stages run every time a new candidate model appears, as opposed to every week on production data?
options: Drift check and retrain trigger
Train, gate, register, and serve with a contract test
Only the retrain trigger
Only the drift check
questions.explain: Stages 1 to 4 (train, gate, register, serve and contract-test) run per candidate. Stages 5 and 6 (drift check and retrain decision) run weekly on live data.

questions.q: In this capstone, which part is illustrative rather than run for real?
options: The local MLflow registry
The validation gate
The GitHub Actions workflow, which was checked to parse but not run on GitHub
The drift check
questions.explain: Every pipeline stage runs locally. Only the GitHub Actions workflow is illustrative: it parses as valid YAML, but it was not executed on GitHub.

questions.q: The baseline model scores ROC AUC 0.744 and average precision 0.333, while a no-skill dummy model scores 0.5 and 0.111. Why is average precision 0.111 the no-skill level here?
options: It equals the cancel rate, 0.111, which is what random ranking achieves
Because the dummy model has a bug
Because average precision is always 0.111
Because the test set has 1,200 rows
questions.explain: With about 11 percent of customers cancelling, a model that ranks at random gets an average precision equal to that rate. That is why the floor of 0.25 is more than twice the no-skill level.

questions.q: Why does the capstone use one shared evaluate function for training, the gate, and the monitor?
options: It reduces the number of files in the project
It makes the model more accurate
So every stage computes metrics the same way and they can never disagree
It is required by scikit-learn
questions.explain: If training, gating, and monitoring each computed AUC differently, a model could pass one check and fail another for reasons that have nothing to do with quality.
